RESUELLO, CPA Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, 3rd District Tuguegarao City, Province of Cagayan Dear SP Member Resuello: This refers to your letter dated May 16, 2023 requesting guidance on the legal implications of the legislative actions taken by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Cagayan during its 42nd Regular Session. As represented in your letter,this Department has sent a letter to your good Office re: Appointment as Acting Vice Govemor of Cagayan dated April 26, 2023, in connection with the 'alleged' travel abroad on May 6-14, 2023 of the Governor. Apparently, your good Office has not received a copy of a similar letter and thus lacks knowledge of said order until [May 16, 2023]. You intimated that due to your lack of knowledge of such travel, you did not perform your duties and functions as Acting Vice Governor. Hence, during the 42nd Regular Session of the 11th Sanggunian on May 10, 2023, held at the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Session Hall, you attended the session and exercised your duties and functions as Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member/Floor Leader instead of Acting Vice Governor—following this Department's Order. During the said Regular Session, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Cagayan has considered various items in its Agenda, which includes "Resolutions Approving Provincial Development Councl (PDC) No. 07, series of 2022 entitled 'A Provincial Development Council Adopting the Provincial Development Investment Program (PDIP) CY 2023-2028 and Indorsing the Same to the August Sangguniang Panlalawigan for Appropriate Action" which has been acted favorably by the Provincial Board through the approval of Resolution No. 2023-11-275 entitled "A Provincial Development Council (PDC) No. 07 series of 2022 entitled: 'A Provincial Development Council Adopting the Provincial Development Investment Program (PDIP) CY 2023- 2023 and Indorsing the Same to the August Sangguniang Panlalawigan for Appropriate Action" crucial legislative action xxx of the deliberation leading to the approval and authorization of the CY 2023 Annual Executive budget." Foremost, it is to be established at the outset that there is a temporary vacancy in the office of the Local Chief Executive last May 6-14, 2023, in light of the incumbent Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Governor's travel abroad during such a period. This warrants automatic succession pursuant to Section 46(a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code). In such a case, the vice governor shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive. Consequently, the exercise of the powers and performance of the duties and functions of the Governor by the Vice Governor during such a period—in this case, from May 6 to 14, 2023—creates a corresponding temporary vacancy in the latter's office during such a contingency. Under such circumstances, Item IV (B)(I) of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21 (Operational Guidelines and Rules in Implementing Administrative Order No. 15, series of 2018) finds application. It provides: "When a temporary vacancy exists in the office of the vice-governor or city or the highest ranking sangguniang municipal vice mayor panlalawigan/panlungsod/bayan member, as the case may be, shall be designated by the President, through the SILG or the OIC-DILG immediately upon the report of the concerned DILG Regional Office of the said vacancy, as acting provincial vice governor or city or municipal vice mayor. He/She shall exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the office except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss officials and employees in the sangguniang panlalawigan/panlungsod/bayan which can only be exercised if the temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days." (Emphasis supplied) This Department submits that your lack of notice or knowledge of your Designation Order as Acting Vice-Governor is a sufficient justification for your non-performance of duties and functions of an Activing Governor. It settled that legislative acts enjoy the presumption of validity and that legislative bodies are presumed to have carried out their function regularly in enacting the said measures, pursuant to Rule 131, Section 3(m) of the Rules of Court. In the case of Municipality of San Mateo, Isabela v. Smart Communications, Inc. (G.R. No. 219506, dated June 23, 2021), the Supreme Court held that the courts accord the presumption of constitutionality to legislative enactments, including municipal ordinances. This presumption may be set aside only when invalidity or unreasonableness appears on the face of the ordinance, or is established by proper evidence. The same is true in the case of City of Cagayan de Oro v. CEPALCO (G.R. No. 224825, dated October 17, 2018), where the Supreme Court held that the presumption of validity may be rendered naught when the invalidity or unreasonableness of an ordinance is ostensibly apparent. Accordingly, the various Resolutions and actions that you palticipated in as Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member/FIoor Leader instead of Acting Vice Governor are accorded such presumption of validity, unless evidence to the contrary is presented. This opinion is being rendered based on the facts as represented and without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, Page 2 of 2

By the Aut ty ATTY. JUAN V Under the Secretary: or rna egal and Legislative Affairs OUSELIAJVULL LRALLD0am/clp Dir. AGNES DE LEON, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG 2 Regional Government Center, Carig Sur, Tuguegarao City, Cagayan Page 2 of 3
